title: Primary biliary cholangitis: immune bile-duct attack like GVHD
vignette: A 52-year-old woman is evaluated for a 6-month history of progressive fatigue and generalized pruritus. She has had no significant prior medical conditions or surgery and takes no medications. The patient does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. Her sister has Sjögren syndrome. Physical examination shows skin excoriations and mild hepatomegaly. Laboratory results show an alkaline phosphatase of 480 U/L (normal 30-120), aspartate aminotransferase (SGOT) 37 U/L, alanine aminotransferase (SGPT) 49 U/L, and a positive antimitochondrial antibody. The pathogenesis of this patient's disease process most closely resembles that of which of the following conditions?

clues.note: Fatigue and pruritus are the classic early symptoms of cholestasis in primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), driven by impaired bile flow and retained bile constituents.
PBC clusters with other autoimmune diseases (Sjögren, rheumatoid arthritis, thyroiditis). A family/personal autoimmune history supports an autoimmune, immune-mediated liver disease.
A markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (480 / normal 30-120 U/L) with near-normal AST (37) and ALT (49) is a CHOLESTATIC pattern - injury centered on bile ducts, not hepatocytes.
Antimitochondrial antibody is the serologic hallmark of PBC (positive in most cases), confirming autoimmune destruction of small intrahepatic bile ducts.

whatMatters: Middle-aged woman + pruritus/fatigue + cholestatic labs (very high ALP, near-normal AST/ALT) + positive antimitochondrial antibody + autoimmune family history = primary biliary cholangitis. PBC is autoimmune, lymphocyte-mediated destruction of small intrahepatic bile ducts. That immune mechanism most resembles GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST DISEASE, where donor T cells attack host bile-duct epithelium. Answer D.
strategy: Diagnose PBC (AMA+, cholestatic pattern, autoimmune woman), then abstract the MECHANISM: T-cell/lymphocytic immune destruction of small intrahepatic bile ducts. Ask which listed disease shares that immune bile-duct attack -> GVHD (donor T cells target host bile ducts). Reject the toxic/metabolic/vascular causes (acetaminophen, alcohol, Budd-Chiari, hemochromatosis, Reye), which share labs superficially but not mechanism.

eliminations.label: Acetaminophen toxicity - direct hepatocellular necrosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: dose-dependent centrilobular hepatocyte necrosis from NAPQI. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a toxic hepatocellular injury with massive transaminase elevation - not immune bile-duct destruction. ✅ Correct if: acute hepatocellular injury with sky-high AST/ALT.

eliminations.label: Alcohol-induced hepatitis - toxic hepatocyte injury
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hepatocellular swelling/necrosis with steatosis, Mallory bodies, neutrophils; AST:ALT >2:1. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's toxic, not autoimmune cholangitis. ✅ Correct if: alcoholic liver disease.

eliminations.label: Budd-Chiari syndrome - venous outflow obstruction
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hepatic vein/IVC occlusion causing congestion and centrilobular necrosis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a VASCULAR process, not immune bile-duct injury. ✅ Correct if: hepatomegaly + ascites from venous thrombosis (e.g., hypercoagulable state).

eliminations.label: Hemochromatosis - iron overload
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: excess iron deposition (hemosiderin) in hepatocytes (genetic/metabolic). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a metabolic deposition disease, not autoimmune cholangitis. ✅ Correct if: iron-overload cirrhosis with high ferritin/transferrin saturation.

eliminations.label: Reye syndrome - mitochondrial hepatotoxicity
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: microvesicular steatosis + encephalopathy in children after aspirin during a viral illness. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: unrelated mechanism and population. ✅ Correct if: pediatric aspirin-associated hepatic failure.

reasoning: Positive antimitochondrial antibody + cholestatic labs + autoimmune woman = primary biliary cholangitis
PBC = immune (T-cell) destruction of small intrahepatic bile ducts
Graft-versus-host disease similarly features donor T-cell attack on host bile-duct epithelium
-> shared immune bile-duct injury; answer D
mechanism: Primary biliary cholangitis is a chronic autoimmune liver disease in which T-lymphocyte-mediated (and antimitochondrial antibody-associated) injury destroys small and medium intrahepatic bile ducts, producing cholestasis (elevated alkaline phosphatase, pruritus, fatigue) with relatively preserved transaminases; it predominates in middle-aged women and clusters with other autoimmune conditions such as Sjögren syndrome. Histology shows patchy lymphocytic (granulomatous) destruction of bile ducts (florid duct lesion). Among the options, only graft-versus-host disease shares this immunologic mechanism: after allogeneic hematopoietic transplant, donor T cells recognize host tissues - including biliary epithelium - as foreign and destroy small intrahepatic bile ducts, raising alkaline phosphatase. The other options are toxic (acetaminophen, alcohol, Reye), vascular (Budd-Chiari), or metabolic (hemochromatosis), and do not share the autoimmune bile-duct mechanism.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid GI > PBC: antimitochondrial antibody, cholestatic pattern (↑ALP), autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts, middle-aged women; GVHD immunology.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: The question asks for a shared MECHANISM, not the diagnosis - abstract PBC to 'immune bile-duct destruction' and match it to GVHD.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on antimitochondrial antibody, cholestatic, alkaline phosphatase, or graft-versus-host disease? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: The other liver diseases share elevated liver labs superficially but are toxic/metabolic/vascular - none is an immune attack on bile ducts like PBC and GVHD.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: AMA+ + high ALP + pruritus in a middle-aged woman = PBC; immune (T-cell) bile-duct destruction, mechanistically like GVHD.
